narrative.intro: Thalle Construction reports $1.9B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Thalle Construction received 3 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $638M, and obligations are up 571.1% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations earlier in the decade were $167M in FY21, $213M in FY22, $16.1M in FY23, $366M in FY24, and $285M in FY25. The Department of Defense obligated $1.9B to Thalle Construction in FY2026 to date. The Department of the Interior obligated $114K. Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction accounts for $1.9B of Thalle Construction’s obligations this fiscal year. Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction accounts for $114K. All figures reported are contract obligations except award-value figures in the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables, which are total contract values. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date figures. The company’s FY2026 activity is concentrated in heavy and civil engineering work for the Department of Defense, with a small amount of water and sewer work for the Department of the Interior.

sections.heading: Who are Thalle Construction's biggest federal customers?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the largest buyer for Thalle Construction, obligating $1.9B in FY2026 to date. The Department of the Interior is a much smaller buyer, obligating $114K. Together these agencies account for the FY2026 obligations listed for Thalle Construction.

sections.heading: What types of work does Thalle Construction sell to the government?
sections.body: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction is the primary market for Thalle Construction, accounting for $1.9B in FY2026 to date. Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction accounts for $114K, indicating a small amount of water and sewer-related work.
